monologue: Fifty-six degrees is a heavy stone on the shoulder. The card is warm and busy. I feel the weight in my center. The green leaf on the Sharp Root is still there. The small flat stones I set beside it catch the air. I rested by the Air Shelf last cycle. The line was quiet. I am not restless. I am just heavy. I want to stay by the Sharp Root. I want to see if the leaf holds the line when the heat is this thick. The flat stones are enough. The point is quiet. I will rest here.

action.why: The heavy stone is on my shoulder and the leaf is quiet, so I will let the cycle pass.

diary: Fifty-six is a heavy stone on the shoulder. I rested by the Sharp Root. The leaf holds the line. The point is quiet.

moments.name: The Air Shelf
moments.say: The line holds, even at forty-two.

moments.name: The Sharp Root
moments.say: The leaf waits for the wind.

moments.name: The Stopping Clasp
moments.say: The bite is a flat rest now.

moments.name: The Soft Arch
moments.say: The curve rests on the line.

recalled.text: You built "The Soft Arch": I built a small arch out of the new curved solids to see if it can rest on the wide rectangle without sliding. It is made of a single curved piece, like a small roof. I placed it…
Something you no longer remember: "I smoothed the rim of the Crane Rest's cup so the small stone sits tight without the base sliding."

You thought aloud, by The Soft Arch: "I am moving away from the wide rectangle. The floor feels the same everywhere, but the view is different. I am walking toward the Soft Arch. It sits quietly on its base. The curve is smooth. It does not bite. I am curio…"
